newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Benguet 9-mth net loss 462.7 mln pesos.
newsitem.headline: Benguet 9-mth net loss 462.7 mln pesos.

text.p: Philippines' Benguet Corp reported a 462.7 million peso net loss in the first nine months of the year, worse than the 87.9 million peso loss registered in the same period last year, the company said on Thursday.
The 462.7 million peso loss excluded extraordinary gains of 371.5 million pesos.

Part of the one time gains came from the sale of its Paracale gold operation's mill facilities which fetched 100.9 million pesos and 256.6 million pesos it received as option payment for its Kingking copper-gold operation.
With the non-recurring gains, the company posted a net loss of 91.2 million pesos as compared with 74.0 million peso net loss last year.
The company posted a non-recurring gain of 13.9 million pesos in the same nine-month period last year.
Operating revenues slipped to 1.952 billion pesos, down from 2.235 billion pesos in the same period last year.

In the third quarter alone, the company registered a net loss of 375.6 million pesos, stripped of extraordinary gains, as compared with 105.1 million peso loss in the same three month period last year.
Operating loss from its Dizon mine ballooned to 56.4 million pesos in the third quarter, from year-ago's 19.2 million pesos due to decline in copper prices and landslides.

"The downturn in copper, coupled with slides at the southeast/southwest portions of the Dizon open-pit mine which entailed unanticipated clean-up costs and limited access to the better grade ore, led to a loss for the Dizon Copper-Gold operation," Benguet president Dennis Belmonte said in a statement.
The company also had to keep its Benguet Antamok mine operation closed during the entire quarter due to opposition from small-scale miners. The mine was reopened November 2.
In the third quarter, the mine posted a net loss of 101.7 million pesos from a net loss of 26.8 million pesos during the year-earlier period.
Its Masinloc chromite operation earned 2.1 million pesos in the third quarter, lower than the year-ago 4.4 million pesos.
The company is the country's oldest mining company. It produces gold, copper concentrates and chromite.
Benguet said it was still looking for investors interested in its gold mine operation in Benguet.
"The Benguet mine is in the market for potential investors either on an outright sale or joint venture arrangement," the company said.
The Paracale mining facility was sold to Base Metals Mineral Resources Corp (BMMR) on August 8. The buyer paid Benguet 97.8 million pesos.
Under the agreement, BMMR will have the option to buy the mining rights for a price of 297.2 million. The option will lapse on September 30, 1999.
Exploration works are still in progress at its Kingking Mines by partners Echo Bay Mines Ltd and TVI Pacific Inc.

"The initial results of Echo Bay's work have increased the ore reserves from 315 million tonnes with a grade of 0.44 percent total copper and 0.52 g/t gold to 529 million tonnes with a grade of 0.35 percent total copper and 0.41 g/t gold," the company said.
Belmonte said the resumption of the Benguet-Antamok and better access to the Dizon mines should help improve the company's earnings performance in the fourth quarter.
Bank loan obligations continued to plague the company, with principal loan amortisation totalling about 484 million pesos every year up to year 1998.
At the same time, Benguet said it was looking at its real estate holdings for possible development.
"This is in line with current investment trends in the Philippines where real estate has become a highly marketable commodity among local and foreign investors," the company added.
